title: New York's Erasing Borders Dance Festival Returns for 18th Year With Seven Classical Indian Forms
excerpt: The Indo-American Arts Council's flagship event brings Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Mohiniyattam, and more to Hunter College on September 19–20.
body:
• The 18th Annual Erasing Borders Dance Festival takes place September 19–20, 2026, at The Kaye Playhouse at Hunter College in Manhattan.
  • The two-evening program features performances across seven classical and contemporary Indian dance forms, including a rare Kalaripayattu martial-arts set.
  • Tickets start at $20, making it one of the most accessible Indian performing-arts events in New York.
  • A free lecture at the New York Public Library on September 24 rounds out the festival programming.

The Indo-American Arts Council will host the 18th Annual Erasing Borders Dance Festival on September 19 and 20, 2026, at The Kaye Playhouse at Hunter College on Manhattan's Upper East Side. The two-evening program begins at 6 PM each night and showcases an unusually broad range of Indian classical and contemporary dance traditions.

What to Expect on Stage

Saturday's lineup opens with a Bharatanatyam duo by Ganesh Vasudev and Nitya Narasimhan, followed by a Kuchipudi solo from Sreelakshmy Kallungal Govardhanan and a Kathak trio led by Shila Mehta alongside Salonee Satagar and Sanchita Dighe. Preeti Vasudevan presents a contemporary solo, and the evening closes with Radhe Jaggi and Team performing a combined Bharatanatyam and Kalaripayattu set — a rare pairing that blends South India's oldest classical dance form with its oldest martial art.

Sunday features Radha Varadan in a Kathak solo, Dr. Neena Prasad and musicians in a Mohiniyattam group performance, Aparna Sindhoor and Anil Natyaveda presenting Sindhoor Natya in a Navarasa group piece, and Arushi and Sawani Mudgal in an Odissi trio.

"Experience the magic of the festival by reserving your tickets for this unforgettable two-night celebration."

— Indo-American Arts Council

A Festival With Deep Roots

Erasing Borders has been New York's premier Indian dance festival since its founding by the Indo-American Arts Council, a nonprofit that has championed South Asian arts across the five boroughs for over two decades. The festival's name reflects its mission: bridging the cultural distance between Indian classical traditions and American audiences while giving US-based Indian dance companies a marquee platform.

This year's roster spans seven distinct forms — Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Mohiniyattam, Kalaripayattu, and contemporary — making it one of the broadest single programs the festival has staged.

Beyond the Stage

The festival extends beyond the two performance nights. On September 24, the Fifth Annual Dr. Sunil Kothari Lecture takes place at the Bruno Walter Auditorium at the New York Public Library for the Performing Arts. This year's lecture, titled "The Balanced Dance as a Journey Towards Inner Stillness and Equanimity," will be delivered by Bharatanatyam artist Rama Vaidyanathan.

Tickets and Logistics

Tickets start at $20 and are available through the IAAC website. The Kaye Playhouse is located at Hunter College, 68th Street between Park and Lexington Avenues — accessible via the 6 train to 68th Street–Hunter College.

For the Indian diaspora in the New York metro area, the festival represents a rare chance to see multiple classical traditions performed at a professional level in a single weekend. The $20 entry price undercuts most comparable performing-arts events in Manhattan by a wide margin.
